title: Cold rebuild: a liveness probe that kills a healthy app
summary: Fix a restart loop caused by a wrong probe on a real Kubernetes cluster, from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *probes* you stopped a liveness probe from killing a healthy app and added a readiness
probe, on a real cluster. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The
checks are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; doing it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Your liveness probe calls `/health`, which checks the database. The database has a 30-second outage. What happens?
options: Every replica fails liveness and is restarted, turning a short DB blip into a full outage and restart storm
Pods are removed from the Service until the DB returns, then come back
steps.explain: Liveness should check only the process itself. Put dependency checks in **readiness**, and even there be careful: if all replicas go unready at once, the Service has no endpoints.

steps.title: A liveness probe that kills a healthy app, cold
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`).
`api` (whoami, `GET /health` on port 80) keeps restarting because of its liveness probe. Fix the liveness probe and
add a readiness probe on `/health`, so the new pod stays up without restarts and is Ready.
From memory: no hints this time.
